question: A B-Lynch brace suture is placed to manage atonic PPH that has not responded to uterotonic drugs. The haemostatic mechanism of this suture is:

answers.text: Ligation of the uterine arteries at their origin from the internal iliac arteries

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Internal iliac artery ligation is a separate, technically demanding procedure targeting the vascular supply; the B-Lynch suture works through mechanical compression, not vascular ligation.

answers.text: Mechanical compression of the uterine body, reducing sinusoidal blood flow at the placental bed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The B-Lynch suture applies sustained longitudinal compression to the uterine body, collapsing the intramural sinusoids and allowing haemostasis to occur. It preserves uterine vascularity and future fertility.

answers.text: Obliteration of the uterine cavity by apposing the anterior and posterior uterine walls

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This description better fits a Cho square suture, which places interlocking sutures to compress specific bleeding areas, not the B-Lynch brace suture.

answers.text: Devascularisation of the placental bed by compressing the broad ligament

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The B-Lynch suture does not compress the broad ligament and does not primarily devascularise the placental bed. Its mechanism is myometrial compression.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the B-Lynch brace suture technique. Its mechanism is sustained mechanical compression of the uterine body, reducing flow through the placental bed sinusoids — distinct from arterial ligation or square sutures.
Well done. The B-Lynch suture achieves haemostasis through mechanical compression of the uterine sinusoids, not vascular ligation or cavity obliteration.
